comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C35-C38, C97-C99 regarding tumor/LN overlap being higher than tumor/PBMC overlap. Both evaluations find the evidence well-supported with appropriate statistical testing. Reviewers explicitly describe this as providing 'useful insights' that 'will inform future study design.'
Perfect agreement on claims C4, C85-C86 regarding expanded clonotypes having fewer mutations. Both evaluations accept these findings as valid contributions without methodological concerns.

Perfect agreement on claims C6, C92-C95, C112 regarding CDR-H3 property differences between clonal and non-clonal populations. Both evaluations support the evidence for pre-SHM selection. Reviewers specifically identify this as 'a particular strength of the study.'

Strong agreement on claims C78-C80, C82-C84 regarding intratumoral heterogeneity and TLS formation. Both evaluations accept the repertoire heterogeneity data and histological validation. Reviewers explicitly praise these findings as 'of importance' for understanding the TME.

Strong agreement on claims C39-C42 regarding isotype-specific overlap patterns (IgG vs IgA). Both evaluations accept the differential trafficking patterns as valid data-driven conclusions. Peer review also includes C104 which OpenEval addresses separately in R8.

Agreement on claims C43 and C45 regarding clonality and isotype correlations. Both evaluations accept these as valid observations. OpenEval also addresses C44 which is not explicitly mentioned in peer review.

Agreement on claims C65-C66 regarding cancer-type-specific hypermutation differences in lung cancer. Both evaluations accept the data, though both note the interpretation linking to tumor mutational load is speculative.

Agreement on claims C67-C69 regarding clonal group tissue distribution patterns. Both evaluations accept these as valid observations without methodological concerns. OpenEval also addresses C104-C105 which are not explicitly mentioned in this peer review result.

Agreement on claims C89-C91 regarding phylogenetic analysis and lack of correlation between CDR-H3 properties and tree position. Both evaluations accept these findings and the acknowledged limitations of short-read sequencing. OpenEval also addresses C87-C88 which peer review covers in R14.

Strong agreement on claims C51-C56, C63, C103 regarding Kidera factor analysis showing CDR-H3 property differences. Both evaluations support the data but note mechanistic interpretations rely on cited literature. Reviewers specifically highlight 'detailed CDR3 physicochemical properties analysis' as 'a particular strength.'

Agreement on claims C30, C32, C96 regarding bulk BCR repertoires resembling plasma cell repertoires. Both evaluations accept this validation as methodologically sound. OpenEval also addresses C31, C33-C34 which peer review covers separately in R13.

Agreement on claims C49-C50, C102 regarding cancer-type-specific CDR-H3 length differences in colorectal cancer. Both evaluations accept the data but acknowledge the microbiota interpretation is speculative. OpenEval addresses broader CDR-H3 length analysis (C46-C48, C100-C101) not explicitly mentioned in this peer review result.

Agreement on claims C70-C72 regarding LN-to-LN heterogeneity in colorectal cancer patient ccp2. Both evaluations accept the differential overlap data, though both note the interpretation about 'inequality in access to tumor antigens' is inferential.

Agreement on claims C73-C74, C109 regarding intra-LN heterogeneity. Both evaluations strongly support these findings. Reviewers explicitly state these findings 'are of importance, contribute to the understanding of the TME, and will inform future study design.'

Partial agreement on claims C46-C49, C100-C101 regarding CDR-H3 length analysis. Both evaluations support the statistical findings. Reviewers praise the 'detailed CDR3 physicochemical properties analysis' as a strength, though they also emphasize the broader interpretation about less-specific repertoires (C5, C63).
Agreement on claims C33-C34 regarding IgM underrepresentation in bulk tumor samples. Both evaluations accept this as a notable exception to the general plasma cell resemblance finding.

Agreement on claims C87-C88 regarding phylogenetic tree validation using short vs long sequences. Both evaluations accept the correlation analysis and acknowledge sequencing limitations appropriately.
Agreement on claim C113 regarding acknowledged limitations in sequencing methodology. Both evaluations accept this as appropriate scientific caution about technical constraints.

Agreement on claims C2-C3 regarding spatial heterogeneity as core findings. Both evaluations strongly support these novel observations about LN-to-LN and intra-LN heterogeneity. Reviewers explicitly praise these findings as important contributions to understanding the TME.

Agreement on claim C5 regarding tumor repertoires showing less stringent control than PBMC. Both evaluations support the CDR-H3 property data. Reviewers specifically endorse the interpretation of 'less-specific BCR repertoire of TIL-B compared to circulating B cells' as a strength, while OpenEval notes the mechanistic interpretation is inferential.
